title: Things people order or book while some are left: products with stock, workshops and classes with seats, races with places
about: A shop's shelf, a studio's workshops, a club's races: each row a card with its photo, date, price and how many are left. A few left says 'Only 2 left'; none says the out word ('Sold out', 'Full') and offers no action; the rest offer the action, which opens the view that finishes the order or booking with {id} (open), or calls a rule with {id} that checks and lowers the count in one step (call: give the rule a REQUIRE, so two people never get the last one). For dated rows, where 'day >= :today' and order 'day' keep the coming ones, soonest first. Use it on a front page or a booking screen: a visitor sees what is on offer, never a form that edits rows.

table.about: the table of things to order or book

eyebrow.about: a short line above the heading

name.about: the column with each one's name

text.about: a column with a line about each one

image.about: a column with its photo (a URL or a file's id)

left.about: the column with how many are left (stock, seats, places)

date.about: a column with its day or time, shown on the card

where.about: an SQL condition on the rows (:today is today)

soon.about: from how many left the card says 'Only N left'

open.about: the view that finishes the order or booking, opened with {id}

call.about: the function or rule called with {id} instead, when one tap is the order (a booking for the signed-in person)

done.about: what the toast says after a call

{{key}}.sql: SELECT * FROM {{table}}{{where|pre: WHERE }} ORDER BY {{order}} LIMIT 60

let.{{key}}_act: =item => ({{open|json}} ? {label: {{action|json}}, open: {{open|json}}, params: {id: item.id}} : {label: {{action|json}}, do: async () => { await app.call({{call|json}}, {id: item.id}); app.toast({{done|json}}); }})

then.text: Nothing on offer right now. Check back soon.
